applies_why: The judge text resolves a collision between pressed chains by treating the absence of a verse that names the body-channel as leaving the point open, which is the verse-by-verse stating-verse inquiry the rule governs.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: 'never verse by verse' / retired stating-verse test. I weighed whether 'without naming whose body is the channel' is a forbidden demand that a verse state the channel in its own words, or a permissible footing conclusion that the chain leaves the channel open.
why: The judge resolves the collision by noting that the text does not name the channel in its own words, rather than weighing the parties' chains by footing, so it applies the retired stating-verse/verse-by-verse test.
